chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, who said:
Someone who saw Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام at Minā informed me that he was wiping the top of his feet, from the upper part of the foot to the ankle, and from the ankle to the upper part of the foot.

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ: Abū al-Ḥasan, the Imam عليه السلام mentioned in the report
key_terms.أَعْلَى الْقَدَمِ: the upper part of the foot
key_terms.بِمِنًى: at Minā, the location where the Imam عليه السلام was seen
key_terms.ظَهْرَ قَدَمَيْهِ: the top of his two feet
key_terms.يَمْسَحُ: he was wiping, referring to the act of masḥ in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: How did Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام wipe his feet in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith reports an observed description of the Imam’s wudu (ablution), specifically his wiping over the top of the feet. It is significant in discussions of ritual purity and the legal details of wudu (ablution) in Shia fiqh.
